findings.issue: All loaders return Promise<any> and every component consumes data: any, so the server/client data contract is entirely untyped; renaming a view-model field or typoing a sort key fails silently.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for each loader's return shape and type the route components' props against them; TypeScript is already configured, this is the only typing in the codebase.

findings.issue: The `<Show when={data()} fallback={<Show when={data() === null}><NotFound/></Show>}>` pattern is duplicated verbatim in four route files (moves:16, abilities:15, types:15).
findings.suggestion: Extract a small `DataOrNotFound` wrapper component that takes the async resource and renders children or NotFound.

findings.issue: The type-API-name-to-English-name map is built inline in loadHomeData, duplicating getTypeNameMap (api.ts:46-48).
findings.suggestion: Call getTypeNameMap() (it's already fetched alongside the other data) instead of rebuilding Object.fromEntries.

findings.issue: Sortable columns are keyed by raw strings matched against any-typed rows, so a mismatch between COLUMNS keys and DTO fields silently disables sorting for that column.
findings.suggestion: Type the rows and derive COLUMNS from the row interface, or key columns by accessor functions instead of strings.

findings.issue: One 303-line route file holds PokemonPage, EvoNode, PokemonDetail, MovesSection and MoveTable; the moves machinery is cohesive but will grow in place.
findings.suggestion: Extract MovesSection/MoveTable into components/moves/ once any change to them is needed; today the split point is obvious so cost is low.

summary: This is a well-structured SolidStart 2 app: thin routes over server-side query/loaders, all API access and caching behind a single seam in lib/api.ts, and genuine shared abstractions (toSpeciesCards, PokemonCard) that cover the app's real variation. Every measured scenario lands in one or two obvious files. The main editability debt is the total absence of types on the data contract plus a few small copy-paste patterns, which cost compiler safety rather than locality.
